description: MLSys review: the ~85% paid share at n<=2 rests on one boundary with no interval, and it is the largest number in the paper and the one carrying the abstract's headline claim. This measures n=1 across all four D2 boundaries with enough repeats for a real interval, rather than one boundary asserted to generalize.
note_seq_len: Each edge's below/above pair straddles that boundary with a fixed 8-token gap, so real tokens move by a shrinking fraction as the boundary grows (1.6% at 512, 0.2% at 4096) while padded tokens double at every edge -- the same discriminating design as m1_boundary, run at n=1 instead of 4/8 and across all four boundaries instead of one.
note_single_step: Both edges sit far below max_num_batched_tokens=8192 so the scheduler has no reason to split. Every dispatch records its step count and splits are counted, not averaged over: a split reintroduces exactly the smearing this experiment exists to avoid.
note_prediction: cost x~1.02 => padding not paid (cost tracks real tokens). cost x~2.0 => padding paid (cost tracks the compiled bucket).
prediction_mechanism: Target: the paid share of nominal padding at n=1, matched to Table 6's n<=2 row (~85%, no interval). Lever: four boundaries instead of one, 15 repeats instead of 9, so the headline figure gets the same interval treatment as every other row in that table.
